1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Peñaseca for three days. In spring, Lucía Romero's older sister had left for Madrid, and since then Lucía had been running the village's little apothecary shop on her own.
When night fell, she shut the shutters, counted the day's takings, blew out the lamp, and went up to the floor above.
She had barely gone to bed when someone pounded on the downstairs door. A man's voice asked, "Is anyone there?"
On the doorstep stood a young man soaked to the bone, his left arm wrapped in a cloth stained with blood. He said his name was Diego Lobo and that he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need someone to treat me," Lobo said in a low voice. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred reales be enough?"
From his jacket he took out a letter wrapped in waxed paper. "This letter has to reach the monastery of San Blas before the eighteenth of May."
For Lucía, treating that wound would be child's play, but the letter troubled her.
Even so, she refused to take his money and only said, "At dawn tomorrow, I'll take you up to the mountains."
2: At daybreak they set out. Lucía carried a basket on her back with bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope they came upon old Tomás Gil, who was splitting firewood. He set down the axe and told them quietly that the evening before, three strangers had asked at the entrance to the village about a wounded young man.
"Take the trail, Lucía," said Tomás Gil. "The main road isn't safe." Lucía thanked him.
The trail was narrow and slippery. Lucía went ahead, planting each step firmly. Lobo followed her in silence.
By midday the rain had stopped, the mist lifted slowly, and far off the roof of the monastery of San Blas came into view. Waiting at the door was a nun, Sister Inés, in charge of receiving visitors.
Sister Inés took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting 2 years for this letter."
Lobo said to Lucía, "I owe her my life." Lucía smiled. "Then next time you come, fix the roof of the apothecary for me." Lobo stayed at the monastery.
At sundown, Lucía went down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home it was already night; she lit the lamp and sat for a long while behind the counter.
